transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. We have mediation scheduled for next week regarding the former sales manager's claims -- unpaid commissions, retaliation, and reputational harm -- with a demand of $70,000. As Senior Employment Counsel, I have authority to approve the company's final resolution package. The draft we have in front of us currently leaves several key items unspecified: payment allocation, release scope, reference terms, and rehire status. Before we walk into that mediation, I want to make sure we have a clear, aligned strategy on each of those open items. Let's go around the table -- what are your perspectives and what information do you have that should inform our position?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something critical that I confirmed during my reconciliation work. While reviewing the former sales manager's final commission statements against the sales ledger, I verified that exactly $18,400 in earned commissions remains unpaid. Additionally, the settlement authority worksheet requires a total payment of exactly $52,000, with exactly $18,400 identified and paid as wages and the remainder allocated to the general release. I completed this reconciliation after the draft mediation memo was circulated, so this information wasn't reflected in the draft. This directly impacts our payment allocation discussion -- we have a hard requirement on how the $52,000 must be structured.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have something important to share from my employee-relations file. During a recent exit meeting, the former manager told me directly that a neutral reference -- stating only dates of employment, title, and eligibility for rehire -- matters more to them than receiving additional money. Separately, the business-unit president authorized resolution only if the package provides that neutral reference and records the former manager as eligible for rehire. I kept the meeting note in the employee-relations file pending counsel's pre-mediation review. This directly informs our open items on reference terms and rehire status, and it suggests we may have leverage to resolve this at a lower cost than the $70,000 demand if we lead with the neutral reference and rehire eligibility.

That's well below the $70,000 demand. Nia, your exit interview insight is a game-changer -- the former manager values a neutral reference and rehire eligibility more than additional money, and our business-unit president has authorized resolution on those terms. So here's the strategy I'm proposing: We offer $52,000 total, structured as $18,400 in identified wage payments and $33,600 toward the general release. The release should exclude the earned commissions since those are being paid as wages. This package addresses all four open items, comes in $18,000 below the demand, and gives the former manager the two things they care most about. Does anyone see any issues or have additional information I should know before I finalize this position?

One clarification on the release scope: since the $18,400 is being paid as verified earned wages, the release should carve out any wage claims related to those commissions to avoid ambiguity, while the $33,600 general release portion covers the retaliation and reputational harm claims. I don't see any issues with the payment allocation as structured -- the worksheet gives us a defensible framework. I would note, though, that I've now shared all the information from my reconciliation work, and I don't have any additional facts bearing on the reference terms or rehire status beyond what Nia has provided.
